alex: Quick follow-up from the active/active residency RFC — we noticed a corner-case in the lease handoff path that could violate residency if requests are retried across regions.

mika: Yeah saw that in the sim results, can you paste the sequence?

alex: Sequence: client -> edge A (resident) returns 503 -> client retries -> edge B (non-resident) accepts and writes. Resident-constraint violated.

chella: Oof. That's the classic retry-to-nonresident problem. We tried to handle it with X-Resident-Region header, but not all clients propagate it.

dave: Right. Two orthogonal levers: 1) enforce edge-side idempotent routing (reject requests without resident header for certain tenant classes) 2) extend control-plane lease handshake to mark in-flight retries as resident-only for short TTL.

alex: I sketched option 2 in the RFC follow-up doc yesterday. It needs a small flag on the route token and a short-lived sticky marker in the proxy.

mika: Option 1 is easier but will break some public SDK traffic. We need a migration plan.

chella: Migration plan idea: default to permissive for free-tier tenants, strict for enterprise with residency contracts. Roll strict via feature flag + metrics gate.

dave: For option 2, concerns: additional control-plane chatter and operator mental overhead during region drain. Also we need TTL semantics so markers expire on network partitions.

alex: Agree. Marker TTL could be same as lease grace (e.g., 30s) and we log on mismatch. Also add a metric: resident_write_rejects, resident_retry_promotions.

mika: How does this interact with KV cache sharding? If edge B accepts and commits to local cache before control-plane promotion, we could read stale results.

chella: We should sequence commit -> control-plane confirm. Edge B should buffer commit in soft-escrow state until control-plane verifies residency. If mismatch, we tombstone the local commit and handoff to resident.

dave: That sounds heavy. Maybe keep it simpler: synchronous verify for writes that touch PII/residency-sensitive flags, asynchronous for others.

alex: Yeah tiered consistency. We already classify tenants by residency sensitivity. So enforce sync-verify for high-sensitivity tenants only. Lower sensitivity follows eventual residency reconciliation.

mika: Operators will want clear runbook steps: how to detect thrown-away local commits and how to replay to resident region. Can we surface an index of orphaned commits?

chella: We can tag escrowed commits with a global id and expose a reconciliation queue in Console. Add a new telemetry event: escrowed_commit_expire -> reconciliation_job_created.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Rolling canary for proxy v1.14 containing residency-marker logic scheduled at 2024-10-03T14:00Z :rocket:

alex: Action items: 1) I will update the RFC with TTL values and escrow lifecycle (owner: alex). 2) Mika, prototype proxy flag and local marker handling (owner: mika). 3) Chella, draft operator runbook and console telemetry (owner: chella). 4) Dave, assess control-plane load impact (owner: dave).

mika: One more Q — what about SDKs adding header automatically? Might be the least invasive long-term fix.

chella: We should coordinate SDK changes but cannot rely on all third-party clients. So server-side fixes remain primary.

dave: Agreed. We'll treat SDK header as augmentation.

alex: OK, let's sync up Thursday 10am PT to validate the proto and metric hooks.

mika: Sounds good. Adding meeting invite. :thumbsup:

chella: I'll draft the runbook doc after the meeting and include playbook snippets.

alex: Thanks all.
